title: Gated – White Paper – Canary Building Performance Standards
summary: Learn how municipalities, universities, schools, hospitals, and facility owners can use Building Performance Standards to strengthen asset management, improve capital planning, reduce energy costs, and support long-term compliance.
body_markdown:
What are Building Performance Standards (BPS)?


Building Performance Standards are regulations that require building owners to measure, report, and improve energy performance over time through ongoing performance targets and compliance requirements. Unlike traditional building codes, BPS programs focus on operational performance after construction.


How can facility data improve BPS compliance?


A centralized data foundation provides visibility into building assets, equipment condition, energy use, and maintenance needs, helping organizations prioritize investments, improve reliability, support capital planning, and create a more sustainable path to compliance.


What is Energy Use Intensity (EUI)?


Energy Use Intensity (EUI) measures the amount of energy a building consumes per square foot and is commonly used to evaluate building performance and compliance with Building Performance Standards.


How do Building Performance Standards differ from traditional energy codes?


Building energy codes typically apply during design, construction, or renovation. Building Performance Standards establish ongoing energy-performance targets that building owners must meet throughout a building’s lifecycle.


What strategies can help reduce the cost of BPS compliance?


Organizations can improve compliance through energy benchmarking, asset management, building controls, energy-efficiency upgrades, electrification, and renewable energy investments implemented through a phased strategy.


What is an Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC)?


An Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) allows organizations to implement energy-efficiency improvements with reduced upfront capital requirements. Project costs are repaid over time through the energy savings generated by the improvements.
